topic: Deja Vu: Memory for Coding Agents That Indexes Sessions — Complete Guide

key_points: Open-source (MIT, Go, 816+ stars) zero-dependency CLI + MCP server that turns session logs coding agents already write to disk into a shared memory layer
Retroactive indexing: finds answers from months of sessions recorded BEFORE install (indexing 1,019 sessions / 3.3 GB in ~9.6s; search in ~12ms)
Supports 25 harnesses out of the box: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, opencode, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, Cline, Roo Code, Goose, DeepSeek Harness, Hermes, etc.
Install: curl install.sh | sh + 'deja install --auto'; wires MCP recall + session-start hooks + builds first index in ~ten seconds
Core commands: deja <query>, deja blame <file>, deja fix <error>, deja ctx, deja promote, deja share, deja sync ssh, deja stats --card, deja restore
Marketing/landing site: 'the one memory your coding agents share'
Positioning: every memory tool starts empty and records forward; deja starts full — the transcripts are already the memory, no capture step
Private by construction: indexing/search fully local, keys/tokens/JWTs/PEM private keys stripped at index time, no account, no telemetry
Context efficiency story: reaches same fact coverage as raw-log grep for ~200x fewer tokens (~60x fewer than replaying matched sessions)
Live demo of semantic search over 16 synthetic sessions
Independent review post: frames deja as 'retroactive search and MCP recall over session logs'
Highlights cross-agent handoff: solve in Codex, Claude remembers; a fix found in one agent comes back in any
Noted the compaction survival stat: over 43 compactions, summary keeps 77% of decisions but only 0.2% of commands — deja hands back the other 99.8%
Notes install paths: brew install deja-vu, go install, npx @vshulcz/deja-vu, Scoop on Windows, Claude plugin marketplace
Community demand for Codex global memory ('Add memory functionality similar to Claude code')
Resolution: maintainable global memory via ~/.codex/AGENTS.md file loaded at session init
Illustrates the fragmented, file-based memory landscape the deja approach addresses — each harness solves memory differently
Shows coding-agent memory is an active, unresolved pain point across the ecosystem
Competitor: persistent local markdown memory (daily logs, scratchpad, qmd semantic search) for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor
Emphasis: 'A session records what the agent did. Memory is a judgment about what the next agent should know'
npm install -g myagentmemory; installs skills + hooks per harness
Contrast: forward-capture style (records from install on) vs deja's retroactive indexing

stats.fact: deja indexes ~1,019 sessions / 3.3 GB in ~9.6 seconds, warm search over gigabytes in ~12 ms (median)
Supports 25 coding-agent harnesses out of the box (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, opencode, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, Hermes, and more)
LongMemEval-S benchmark (470 questions): hit@1 85.3%, hit@5 95.5%, MRR 0.896, median search ~25 ms — retrieval-only numbers with in-repo harness
LoCoMo benchmark (1,982 questions): hit@1 69.8%, hit@5 85.8%, MRR 0.768, median search ~7 ms
Context readiness benchmark: deja reaches the same fact coverage as grepping raw logs for ~200x fewer tokens (~60x fewer than replaying matched sessions in full)
Over 43 compactions, agent session summaries keep ~77% of decisions but only ~0.2% of commands run — deja gives back the other 99.8%
Day-zero comparison: deja answered 18/100 at hit@1 on 19,195 sessions built in 29s with a single 18.6 MB binary, no model/key, no background process
Open-source project: 816+ stars, 78 forks, MIT license, one Go binary, actively maintained (1,839+ commits as of Sep 2026)

angles: The 'starts full' advantage: why retroactive session indexing beats every forward-capture memory tool on day one
Stop re-debugging: how deja recall answers 'we fixed this three weeks ago' across different agents (solve in Codex, remember in Claude)
The token/context cost problem: compaction drops 99.8% of commands — deja restores lossless recall without bloating context
Privacy-by-construction: local-only indexing, secrets redacted at index time, no account/no telemetry — why that matters for enterprise codebases
Deja vs the field: honest comparison vs Mem0, Letta, claude-mem, memU, MemPalace, cass — when to pick deja and when a semantic store wins
Hooks that work silently: session-start / PreToolUse / PostToolUse recall means relevant memory arrives before you even ask
Team workflows: deja blame (git blame for the discussion behind code), deja fix, deja share, and SSH cross-machine sync
Set-up walkthrough: 10-second install + 'deja install --auto' → MCP recall wired into every detected agent
